title: Roadmap Launch Readiness - Incident Review
topics: KV cache eviction and prefix caching
summary: Postmortem style review following a 30-45 minute latency spike observed during a canary rollout for the new batching changes. Root cause appears related to unexpected KV cache eviction patterns combined with aggressive autoscaler cooldowns; mitigations include reverting a kernel change, adjusting cache TTLs, and tightening autoscaler thresholds. Next steps: bench and test fixes in staging, update rollout playbook, schedule exec readout.
next_steps: Priya to run KV cache eviction repro and produce logs + timeline (due 2026-04-20)
Carlos to run a focused canary on staging with increased cache retention and conservative autoscaling (start 2026-04-17)

Samir to coordinate exec readout and share postmortem summary (due 2026-04-19)

transcript:
[00:00] Samir (PM): Okay team, start of the incident review, we're 55 minutes on the calendar. thanks everyone for squeezing this in. quick recap: yesterday at 09:12 UTC we saw a 30-45 minute latency spike on production inference for the new batching kernel rollout during canary. effect was increased p95 and some request timeouts.
[00:18] Priya (Eng Lead): Yeah, hi. so prelim analysis points to an interaction between the new kernel scheduler and KV cash — sorry, KV cache — eviction behavior. we saw a bunch of prefix cache misses all at once. the transcriber notes: "kv cash" in the logs, haha.
[00:35] Carlos (SRE): I'll add that autoscaler behavior amplified the problem. during the spike the HPA scaled down some nodes because of a sampling blip; then when the load hit the canary hosts, cold KV loads and repeated recomputation led to token processing backlog.
[00:50] Maya (Product Ops): Can you say why the autoscaler sampled low? was it a metrics delay or a misconfiguration?
[01:02] Carlos: It looks like the metrics source (the exporter on the model pods) had a scrape gap for about 40s, likely due to the pod restart churn from the kernel change. so the HPA cooldown window allowed scale down.
[01:20] Priya: We also had a config tweak in the runtime that changes the KV cache TTL heuristics; that was intended to reduce memory pressure, but combined with the new kernel prefetch timing, we ended up with synchronized evictions. so instead of staggered cache expirations, a lot of keys fell out simultaneously.
[01:40] Evan (Head of Infra): Right, so two orthogonal changes: kernel scheduling and cache TTL heuristics. each was low risk in isolation but together they pushed the canary over the edge.
[01:55] Samir: Did we see any correlation with particular models or sequence lengths?
[02:05] Priya: Mostly long-context requests — 1k+ tokens — because the KV working set is larger; also heavy batching with the new continuous-batching heuristic we shipped. ironically, the batching intended to reduce per-token latency increased tail latency when cache misses spike.
[02:25] Carlos: There were a handful of 504s at the edge LB when the queue depth went over threshold. our retry logic mitigated some, but client-side timeouts caused user-visible errors.
[02:40] Maya: Any impact to Dedicated customers or private deployments?
[02:46] Priya: Minimal, this was only in the hosted canary region. Dedicated pools were unaffected because they have different kernel selection and cache profiles. but worth calling out for communications.
[03:00] Samir: Do we have a short-term mitigation we can push? revert, config change, autoscaler tweak?
[03:08] Priya: Immediate move is to revert the kernel scheduling change for the canary and staging. that brought p95 back within normal range in our rollback test. second, bump KV cache TTL or move to more conservative eviction policy.
[03:22] Carlos: And temporarily increase HPA min replicas and lengthen cooldown to avoid scale-down during transient metric gaps.
[03:32] Evan: I want an explicit revert if staging proves it fixes the issue. we need to avoid half-measures.
[03:38] Samir: Agreed. try revert in staging asap. Priya, can you schedule that?
[03:44] Priya: yes, I'll do a revert today, run the bench, and report back. also will instrument a more detailed eviction log so we can map keys and timestamps.
[03:54] [04:00] (crosstalk, inaudible)
[04:12] Carlos: Also, on the monitoring side, add an alert for synchronized cache miss rate across pods — if multiple pods cross X misses in Y seconds, we flag before p95 climbs.
[04:25] Maya: let's also add a runbook step: if p95>500ms for 5 minutes during a canary, pause rollout and send page to infra oncall.
[04:36] Priya: I'll add that to the launch runbook.
[04:40] Samir: Good. any downstream customers or sales ops noise yet?
[04:45] Maya: no major customer escalations, a few notes in support but nothing that hit execs.
[04:52] Priya: Quick note: logs show the kernel change was a micro-optimization to kernel selection heuristics to prefer fused-attn kernels for short sequences, but the heuristic also changed how KV cache prefetch aligns with kernel batches. it's subtle and we missed the cross-impact locally.
[05:12] Evan: For the roadmap, we need a gating checklist: kernel change must be smoke-tested with KV cache instrumentation and autoscaler load patterns. add that to the release checklist.
[05:24] Samir: action items captured. let's recite next steps. Priya, run KV eviction repro and logs — due 2026-04-20. Carlos run staging canary with increased retention and changed autoscaler — start 2026-04-17. Maya update runbook — due 2026-04-18. Samir schedule exec readout — due 2026-04-19.
[05:52] (wrap up) Maya: I'll create the postmortem doc in confluence and link the bench sheets, will cc infra and product.
[05:58] Samir: thanks everyone. we'll meet again after Priya's logs come in. end.
notes: Observed timing: spike started 2026-04-14T09:12:xxZ, lasted ~35 minutes
Primary suspected causes: kernel scheduling change + KV cache TTL heuristic alignment
Secondary amplifiers: autoscaler cooldown + metrics scrape gap
Immediate mitigation: revert kernel change in canary; increase KV cache TTL; raise HPA min replicas
Longer-term: add gating tests for kernel changes, improved cache instrumentation, automated rollback triggers in runbook
